transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava M (Redwood AE), Daniel C (Redwood SE), Priya R (CSM), Liam (NovaDocs CTO), Maya (Eng Mgr), Ethan (SRE), Sara (Security), Julie (PM - observer)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Liam: Yep this is Liam, hi.
[00:09] Maya: Maya here.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan here.
[00:13] Sara: Sara from security.
[00:15] Ava: Great. So agenda -- onboarding progress, access setup for the dedicated pilot, quick review of the bench run results from last week and then next steps. Daniel, do you want to kick off with results?
[00:28] Daniel: Sure, thanks. So last week's smoke bench we ran on a 4-GPU dev pool, mixed prompt set from NovaDocs that Ethan shared. High-level numbers: avg latency for full prompt+completion was around 280ms median, p95 ~410ms, p99 ~620ms. We saw throughput about 18 tokens/sec per GPU under the current batch config. Cost estimate ballpark was about $0.045 per 1k tokens for the Dedicated config we used - this is beta-ish pricing subject to change.
[00:59] Maya: That p99 620ms, is that with batching on? We need p99 below 400ms for our UI use case.
[01:05] Daniel: Good question. That run had moderate batching (batch size ~8, latency-first policy). We can tune towards latency by reducing batching and enabling prefix KV cache for repeated context - that reduced median in our experiments but it increases per-token cost. There are tradeoffs.
[01:23] Ethan: Can you explain KV cache? We have people calling with similar conversation prefixes.
[01:27] Daniel: Yeah, KV cache keeps the key/value caches across requests so repeated context doesn't re-encode. For chat flows it saves compute and lowers latency for subsequent calls. It's ideally used when calls share a lot of prefix. If your usage is a lot of single-shot prompts, it helps less.
[01:45] Ava: From the product side, we can propose two configs for the pilot: latency-optimized (smaller batch, aggressive KV caching, higher cost) and cost-optimized (larger batching, more efficient kernels/quantization). We'll include per-route estimates.
[01:59] Liam: Sounds good. On infra we hit a blocker - we need to set up VPC peering and be sure our outbound firewall allows Redwood's dev pool IPs. Ethan, can you give status?
[02:09] Ethan: Working on it. I created the service account but haven't opened the firewall rules yet because we wanted the exact IP list. Sara also needs to sign off for security.
[02:18] Sara: Right - security checklist: must ensure traffic is over TLS, no plaintext tokens, keys via our AWS KMS is preferred, logs should be forwarded to our SIEM and audit logs retained for 90 days. Do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:32] Daniel: We support KMS integrations and can do bring-your-own-key. HSM support is available for enterprise Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[02:44] Sara: Good, we'll read that. Also need to confirm RBAC and SSO - we prefer SAML SSO and role-based permissions for who can deploy model rollouts.
[02:56] Priya: We have SAML SSO and RBAC options in the console, and we can provide initial roles for your pilot.
[03:03] Maya: On the dataset side, Liam asked about token mix - we'll send a 5-10MB sample and 20 representative prompts.
[03:11] Liam: Yes, we'll do that today.
[03:13] Ava: Thanks. Back to bench tuning: Daniel, what are the quick levers to bring p99 under 400ms?
[03:20] Daniel: Three main levers: batch policy (reduce target batch size), kv/prefix caching for sessions, and kernel selection/quantization. For your model, switching from 4-bit to a hybrid int8 path improved latency in our earlier runs but there's a quality tradeoff. We can run a side-by-side quality eval on the 1k prompt sample.
[03:40] Ethan: Quality regression worries us - we can't accept hallucination increases.
[03:43] Daniel: Totally. We'll run automatic evals and the Redwood Optimize suggestions will highlight any quality drops tied to quantization. If there's a regression, we can back off to a higher-precision profile.
[03:54] Sara: Also want to confirm audit logs: can we get token-level usage logs masked for PII and retained for 90 days?
[04:02] Ava: Yes, we can provide masked logs and configurable retention. For the pilot we'll enable masking by default and share how to map tokens to request IDs for debug.
[04:12] Maya: Network question - can you do VPC peering or do we need to do private link? We prefer peering if possible.
[04:18] Daniel: We support both. For Hosted we usually recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud provider; for Dedicated we can do peering into your VPC for traffic egress control. We'll provide the peering guide.
[04:30] Ethan: timeline - we want bench run next week if we can get firewall and service account ready.
[04:34] Ava: Daniel, can you allocate the dev pool on 2026-05-06?
[04:37] Daniel: Yes I can do that, I'll put a tentative slot and share the exact window. I'll also prepare the smoke script that runs the 20 prompt set and captures p50/p95/p99 and quality diffs.
[04:48] Liam: Regarding pricing, earlier you said ~$0.045 per 1k tokens. Can you send a breakdown for 3 scenarios - hosted, small dedicated pool, and reserved dedicated?
[04:58] Ava: We will. I'll send the updated pricing sheet showing incremental cost per token and the fixed commit for reserved capacity.
[05:05] Sara: One more security ask - can we get a copy of the SOC2 report and details about where logs are stored (region/residency)? We need EU residency for some data.
[05:15] Ava: We'll share SOC2 plus our data residency options. For Dedicated you can choose region - we'll note EU options.
[05:22] Julie (muted, chat): Can we also capture latency by route? I've put that in chat.
[05:26] Daniel: Yes we'll include per-route latency breakdown in the bench output.
[05:30] Ava: Okay let's recap and confirm owners. Ava will share pricing and peering guide (Ava) by Friday. Daniel will schedule bench and prepare scripts (Daniel). Ethan will open firewall and create service account then confirm. Sara will review security docs and send checklist comments. NovaDocs will send sample dataset and prompt set. Any other asks?
[05:48] Maya: Nothing else.
[05:50] Liam: Nope. Thanks.
[05:51] Ava: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and confirm bench window.
[05:56] End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional dropped words, speaker labels approximate, timestamps every ~15-60s. Some proper nouns slightly off (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cache).
